text:
sre-bot: 🚨 INCIDENT: GPU queue depth for pool 'prod-gpu-a' > 90% for 7m, failed autoscale attempts=3, recent driver Xid errors detected. Pager sent to oncall.

alice: I'm on it. seeing large backlog in the inference queue, clients getting 503/timeout spikes. Paging in infra and runtime.

ben: thx. can someone paste the autoscaler logs? I want to see why it's not provisioning new nodes.

meera: autoscaler shows 'scaleLimitReached' + 'rateLimit: apiQuotaExceeded' from cloud provider around the times of failures. Also some nodes failed to register after boot.

raj: adding runtime team. initial hypothesis: driver regression (recent node image included nvidia-drivers v530.x) causing repeated CUDA Xid 79 and OOM that reduces available GPU capacity -> autoscaler keeps hitting cold-start failures.

alice: confirmed. from one failed node:
```
[2026-03-15T09:41:02Z] nvidia: Xid (79): GPU exception on ch 00000000 d1
[2026-03-15T09:41:05Z] oom-killer: kill process 12345 (python) total-vm: 120000000kB
[2026-03-15T09:41:06Z] kubelet: node status NotReady: driver crashloop
```

meera: also seeing `driver-oom` annotated by node-exporter and then kubelet evicted pods. Evictions spiked and the scaling didn't compensate because provider quota returned 409 on provisioning.

ben: customer impact? support?

support-bot: 3 customer-facing routes reporting elevated latencies (models/lama-13b, models-embed-prod). Top affected orgs: acme-co, beta-startup. No confirmed data loss, errors are 502/504 and throttled requests.

alice: tactical plan: (1) stop routing new requests to prod-gpu-a (failover to prod-gpu-b variant), (2) temporarily lower batch sizes and concurrency on affected routes, (3) cordon one problematic node and attempt driver rollback, (4) open cloud quota escalation with provider.

raj: +1. also run `kubectl drain` on the worst nodes then `systemctl status nvidia-driver` and collect `dmesg | grep -i xid`. If driver rollback fixes crashloop we can roll forward to all nodes.

meera: doing commands now.
```
kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep prod-gpu-a
kubectl drain gpu-node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
ssh gpu-node-17 sudo journalctl -u nvidia-driver -n 200
sudo dmesg | tail -n 50
```

meera: logs from gpu-node-17: multiple Xid 79 events, then a kernel OOM killing `triton-server`. Also saw `nv_peer_memory` errors during init.

ben: that matches the new driver behavior we saw in canaries last week (low freq). Did we flip driver flag in image build on Saturday?

alice: yes, image `inference-node:v2026.03-530` was rolled on Saturday. can we revert to `v2026.02-520` on a trial node?

evan: I can stage a rollback. Will spin up one node with stable image in the same pool and force test invites.

sre-bot: NOTE: autoscaler hit provider quota at 2026-03-15T09:37:10Z, requests failing with 429/409.

meera: rolled back gpu-node-22 to `v2026.02-520` and it's stable so far. `nvidia-smi` shows all GPUs healthy and no Xid messages in dmesg.

alice: good. let's promote that image and cordon/drain remaining suspect nodes one by one, but careful: we only have limited headroom due to quota. plan: (A) failover traffic to prod-gpu-b (B) reduce concurrency on /v1/generate endpoints from 8 -> 4 using runtime feature flags (C) cordon+drain+rollback in small waves.

raj: also enable temporary autoscaler backoff override to allow 1-2 extra nodes if quota becomes available. request sent to cloud-ops to bump limit.

ben: paste the flag change snippet we'll apply to router:```json
{
  "routes": {
    "/v1/generate": { "concurrency": 4 }
  }
}
```

alice: applied patch to router; traffic diverted, requests to lama-13b down 60% on prod-gpu-a. latency improved but still occasional 504s as some pods still crash.

support-bot: notified affected customers with initial ETA: we are mitigating, may be partial degradation for 1-3 hours. PR sent to status page.

meera: continuing node work. node-17 rollback succeeded and rejoined. node-19 still shows `nv_peer_memory` init fail, I'll collect more logs then cordon.

evan: note: autoscaler logs show a race where multiple failed provisioning attempts trigger backoff for 10m. That's what prevented quick replacement of evicted nodes earlier. We should tune backoff config for transient image failures.

alice: good catch. let's reduce backoff to 30s temporarily, so we can retry more quickly as we patch images. raj, can you open a quick PR?

raj: on it. PR title: "temporary autoscaler backoff reduction for incident 2141592653". Adding test and rollback.

ben: any customer action needed beyond notice? Support: prepare credits doc and SLA notes if we cross 30m degradation window.

support-bot: queued escalation to Customer Success for Acme-co and Beta-startup. Draft message ready.

meera: update: after draining 4 nodes and rolling back, pool utilization stabilized at ~60%. No new Xid messages in rolled-back nodes. We still need to patch the image build to remove the problematic driver and re-run canaries.

alice: casualty report: ~12 pods evicted, ~8 failed node boots. No persistent state lost. Estimated customer impact window ~45 minutes. We'll keep status page open.

raj: opened a post-incident ticket for build pipeline: pin driver versions and add smoke tests checking for Xid/oom patterns in canaries.

evan: infra request update: provider increased GPU quota by 4 nodes after manual review. Autoscaler resumed provisioning and finished bringing pools back to desired capacity.

alice: final actions before close: (1) merge rollback PR and re-image remaining nodes, (2) revert temporary backoff tweak after pool healthy, (3) follow up with vendor on driver regression, (4) postmortem and customer impact writeup.

ben: assigning postmortem to me + meera + raj. I'll draft and share within 24h.

sre-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigated -> partial recovery, monitoring. Incident channel will remain open for 2h for checks. :white_check_mark:

alice: thanks team. tagging @support to follow up with the two affected orgs. Please add any missing notes.

support-bot: follow-up messages sent. customers acknowledged and appreciate fast response.

meera: logs/artifacts uploaded to incidents bucket: gs://redwood-incidents/2141592653/ (driver-logs.tar.gz, autoscaler-log-snips.txt, router-patch-diff.txt).

alice: closing thread in 2h unless any regression. great work. :raised_hands:
